facts.claim: High consumption of ultra-processed foods is linked to an increased risk of all-cause mortality in five studies with a risk ratio (RR) 1·25, 95 % CI 1·14, 1·37; P < 0·00001.
facts.quote: highest UPF consumption was found to be associated with increased risk of all-cause mortality in five studies (risk ratio (RR) 1·25, 95 % CI 1·14, 1·37; P < 0·00001)
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

facts.claim: High consumption of ultra-processed foods is linked to an increased risk of irritable bowel syndrome, overall cancer, postmenopausal breast cancer, gestational obesity, adolescent asthma and wheezing, and frailty.
facts.quote: high UPFs consumption was obviously associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality, overall cardiovascular diseases, coronary heart diseases, cerebrovascular diseases, hypertension, metabolic syndrome, overweight and obesity, depression, irritable bowel syndrome, overall cancer, postmenopausal breast cancer, gestational obesity, adolescent asthma and wheezing, and frailty.

facts.claim: High consumption of ultra-processed foods is linked to an increased risk of cerebrovascular disease in two studies with a risk ratio (RR) 1·34, 95 % CI 1·07, 1·68; P = 0·01.
facts.quote: cerebrovascular disease in two studies (RR 1·34, 95 % CI 1·07, 1·68; P = 0·01)

facts.claim: High consumption of ultra-processed foods is linked to an increased risk of depression in two studies with a risk ratio (RR) 1·20, 95 % CI 1·03, 1·40; P = 0·02.
facts.quote: depression in two studies (RR 1·20, 95 % CI 1·03, 1·40; P = 0·02)

facts.claim: Greater exposure to ultra-processed food was associated with a higher risk of adverse health outcomes, especially cardiometabolic, common mental disorder, and mortality outcomes.
facts.quote: Greater exposure to ultra-processed food was associated with a higher risk of adverse health outcomes, especially cardiometabolic, common mental disorder, and mortality outcomes.

rejected.claim: High consumption of ultra-processed foods is linked to an increased risk of subsequent depression with a hazard ratio of 1. 22, 95%CI 1. 16 to 1. 28 in a meta-analysis of prospective studies.
rejected.quote: a meta-analysis of prospective studies demonstrated that greater ultra-processed food intake was associated with increased risk of subsequent depression (hazard ratio: 1. 22, 95%CI 1. 16 to 1. 28)

research.angle: While the sources confirm that ultra-processed foods are linked to various chronic diseases and mental health issues, they do not specifically analyze the chemical additives or inflammatory profiles of granola and protein bars.
research.verdict: The evidence consistently links high consumption of ultra-processed foods to a wide range of adverse health outcomes including mortality, cardiovascular disease, and mental health disorders.
research.caveat: Most of the evidence is derived from observational studies, and large-scale prospective designed studies are still needed to confirm causal pathways.
